title: Vercel Connect: Quickstart and Managed Authorization
summary: Vercel Connect shifts authorization decisions from individual users to organizations, controlling which apps automation workflows can access.
body_markdown:
## Why managed authorization matters to teams automating work


Before any build, settle who may use Vercel Connect. Whoever grants an automation its access decides how much damage a leaked key can do and how long a launch waits.


### Where authorization sits in an AI automation


Each time a step reads or writes another app it needs a credential, and today each automation usually holds its own copies.


The two diagrams below set that against the managed model: on the left, separate keys run from the automation to three apps; on the right, one admin-controlled gate sits between the automation and the same three, so an admin grants and revokes access in one place.


The reason shows in[Verizon's 2025 breach report](https://www.verizon.com/business/resources/reports/2025-dbir-executive-summary.pdf) : **credentials begin 36% of breaches** , so attackers' most reliable entry point is a compromised password or token.


Per Verizon, system intrusion follows at 22%, social engineering at 17%, basic web attacks and miscellaneous errors at 12% each, and privilege misuse at 8%. That means defenders face a landscape where no single control solves the problem.


A stored key is therefore the most common way in, and every extra copy is one more to find and rotate.


### What changes for the admin and what for the builder


On one side the admin gains the approval decision; on the other the builder loses some of the waiting.[WorkOS](https://workos.com/blog/oauth-app-approval-slack-microsoft-atlassian) reports that OAuth app review before org-wide use can take 10 weeks at[Slack](https://slack.green/en/blog/slack-token-rotation) , the team messaging tool.


For Google's restricted scopes, review can take 6 weeks, so securing new scopes requires waiting at least six weeks. It takes 4 weeks for the GitHub Marketplace, which is where GitHub lists approved apps, and 2 weeks for Google's sensitive scopes, per WorkOS.


A builder who needs all of these waits on the slowest, so a plan with a Slack step can stretch past two months.


Nothing in the findings says managed authorization shortens any of those waits. The changelog, the only maker source, describes a change in control, not in timing or cost. **Treat speed and savings as unproven** , and record who owns each connection before anyone builds on it.
